summary: Fixed a floor-editor rendering bug reported right after dropping an appliance on a plan: the marker landed as a bare tone-coloured disc with no icon on it, so a dropped camera and a dropped NVR/IoT hub/door controller looked identical, and neither matched what the placing cursor (and the read-only floor view) show for the same pin. floor_editor.js draws its markers on a , which cannot render an SVG element directly, so each marker glyph is now rasterised once into an from the same shared icon set the palette, the read-only view and the placing cursor already use, cached by name+colour for the life of the page (a cache miss kicks off the load and asks for a redraw when it lands, so the very first frame degrades to the plain disc rather than blocking). The disc grew slightly (camera 7px to 9px radius, appliance 9px to 11px) so a legible glyph fits inside it, drawn in white on the tone-coloured disc - a camera gets the camera icon, an appliance gets its node kind's icon (camera/iot/door). The label's vertical offset now follows the disc radius instead of a hardcoded 13px so the gap above the marker stays constant.
compatibility: Frontend-only rendering fix inside one component (floor_editor.js); no API, schema, i18n, or config changes. The marker hit radius (14px) already comfortably exceeded the new disc size, so click/drag/select behaviour is unchanged. No operator or migration action required. Verified live on a throwaway install with one of each kind pinned on a plan (camera with coverage wedge, NVR, IoT hub, door controller): all four render their own glyph in white on the status-coloured disc and are distinguishable at a glance, matching the read-only view and the placing cursor. Build, go test and npm run lint:undef clean; all four i18n dicts unchanged at an identical key set; zero console errors.
